requirement:
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.

For each `:test:` anchor, the harness MUST include the selected file or node's
source text in the initial model request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` and MUST record that selection
as an evidence input under {cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`,
so changing that source makes the evidence stale.
A `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT require an input selecting its source. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
rationale:
I judge that the marked tests adequately check `requirements.references.anchors`. I did not request implementation source. The obligations and their tests are below.

- **Option syntax, `{req}` and `{example}`.** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchor_options_are_metadata_not_body_text]` parses `:impl:` and `:test:` options only on the lines immediately after the opening fence. It checks that one option per line is recorded, including on a nested example. It also checks that `:impl:` and `:test:` lines later in the body, or inline, stay body text. `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unsupported_and_empty_options_are_validation_errors]` shows `:impl:` on an example is a validation error. Its other cases are an unknown `:phrase:` option on a requirement and an `:impl:` option with no path.
- **Anchors are `{impl}` or `{test}` edges to a file or node.**
  - `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[references_report_anchors_as_file_or_node_sites]` checks the reported sites, whole-file and selector, for both `:impl:` and `:test:` anchors, including the role filter.
  - `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[ripgrep_node_scope_searches_only_the_node_a_selector_anchor_names]` checks that a selector anchor resolves to its node. A stale selector resolves to no node.
  - The `ripgrep_referencing_searches_only_referencing_files_or_nodes` and `ast_grep_referencing_restricts_the_search_as_ripgrep_does` tests in `src/authoring/tools.rs` also cover anchors.
- **Option lines are not definition text and do not render.**
  - `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[requirements_inputs_omit_option_lines]` checks the definition text and the requirements-input text.
  - `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs]` checks the requirements input and `subject_text`. A body line that merely starts with `:impl:` is kept.
  - `anchored_files_must_be_completely_covered_and_resolvable` in `src/evidence.rs` asserts there is no "text changed" error with anchors present.
  - `anchor_options_are_metadata_not_body_text` asserts the option text is absent from rendered output while lookalike body text is kept.
  - `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` asserts the anchor path is not rendered.
- **`:test:` anchors supply source in the initial request and are recorded as evidence inputs.**
  - `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[test_anchors_supply_only_the_selected_node]` checks the node-only input, its hash and its text. It also checks that the prompt contains the target and excludes sibling text.
  - `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs]` checks a whole-file anchor.
  - `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchored_files_must_be_completely_covered_and_resolvable]` checks that a missing input is reported with its line range and that a node-only input does not cover a whole-file anchor.
  - The same test checks that changing the anchored file makes the input stale.
  - `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[selector_anchors_are_covered_by_inputs_selecting_the_node_or_an_ancestor]` checks that the node, an ancestor and the root cover a selector anchor, while a sibling does not.
- **An `:impl:` anchor alone does not require an input.**
  - In `selector_anchors_are_covered_by_inputs_selecting_the_node_or_an_ancestor`, an `:impl:` anchor with empty evidence inputs produces no anchor errors.
  - In `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes]`, the `:impl: src/lib.rs#mod[inner]` source is not contributed as an input.
- **Unresolvable or non-permitted anchors are errors naming the definition and path, and authoring reports them before inference.**
  - `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unreadable_or_denied_anchors_fail_before_inference]` covers a missing file, a missing node in an existing file, and a disallowed path. The first two errors name the requirement and the anchor.
  - `outside_test_anchors_follow_explicit_allow_and_disallow_rules` covers outside-project absolute and parent-relative paths, which are denied by default, allowed by an explicit allow and denied by an explicit disallow.
  - `mandatory_inputs_through_symlinks_leaving_the_project_abort_preparation` covers a symlink that escapes the project.
  - On the validation side, `anchored_files_must_be_completely_covered_and_resolvable` covers a missing path (`missing.sh`) and a disallowed path. `selector_anchors_are_covered_by_inputs_selecting_the_node_or_an_ancestor` covers a missing selector.
- **Path rules.** The outside-path, symlink and disallow tests above cover the `requirements.ci.schema` path rules: project-relative, absolute and parent-relative forms with permission checks.

I found no obligation that lacks a test with an assertion on its outcome. The authoring tests all use requirement subjects, so I found no authoring test with an example subject carrying `:test:` anchors. That path is not a separate requirement-specified distinction, so I do not count it as a gap.

text: :::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
For each `:test:` anchor, the harness MUST include the selected file or node's
source text in the initial model request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` and MUST record that selection
as an evidence input under {cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`,
so changing that source makes the evidence stale.
A `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT require an input selecting its source. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
:::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} roles

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name, or with a built-in name under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, and MAY use the `{fixme}` role in fenced form. A reference MAY instead be written in fenced form, `:::{role} name` on one line, a body, and a closing fence, following the fence rules of {cite}`requirements.ci.span` and {cite}`requirements.ci.fence_lengths`; the fenced form is the same edge with attached commentary, and the inline form carries none. In a source comment, fence lines MUST be recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, and a fence that does not close within its comment run MUST be a validation error. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. The roles MUST mean:
- `{cite}`: the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition. It is an
edge from the source to the definition.
- `{impl}`: the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision,
performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition
specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining
one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or
producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as
implementing it. A check MUST count only if the definition states it, or the
source could not meet one of the definition's obligations without it; source
that checks it is consistent with a definition, such as recognizing a form the
definition specifies in order to decide whether to run other behavior, relies
on that definition and calls for `{cite}`. A requirement stating a convention
for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by
the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that
collects and reports those outputs.
- `{test}`: the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies:
a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome,
or a named example through the concrete case it describes.
- `{fixme}`: the source acknowledges a known gap in fulfilling the definition. It
MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST describe the gap. The body MAY
begin with option lines naming issues that track the gap, one per line, in the
form `:github: <owner>/<repo>#<number>`, such as
`:github: rust-lang/rust#123`. `github` MUST be the only recognized option.
A named `{fixme}` MAY appear only in sources outside the book. Validation MUST report
any other option line, a `:github:` value not in that form, an inline
`{fixme}`, a `{fixme}` in a requirement or example declaration, and a
`{fixme}` whose body, without option lines and comment delimiters, is empty.
An unnamed `{fixme}`, a fence of `:::{fixme}` with no name, MAY appear in any
project text, including a requirement or example body, to tie that place to
the issues it names. It MUST have at least one `:github:` option line and MAY
have a description; it is not a reference edge, acknowledges no gap, needs no
coverage, and does not count as a reference for Rust item coverage. Its
issues are checked under {cite}`requirements.cli.fixme_issues`.
`{impl}`, `{test}`, and `{fixme}` are edges from the definition to the source.
Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the
definitions it implements or tests.

{cite}`requirements.references.roles`
{test}`requirements.references.roles`
:::{req} schema

A requirement or example evidence file at `evidence/<full-name>.json` MUST be a JSON object with exactly `requirement` or `example`, `determination`, `rationale`, `references`, and `inputs`. `references` MUST be the reference-set digest defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`. The definition text and rationale MUST be nonempty strings, `determination` MUST use one of the outcomes defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`, and `inputs` MUST be an array. Every evidence input MUST have exactly one of three forms: an outline input with `file`, `item`, and `hash`; a requirements input with `requirements`, `matches`, and `text`; or a definition input with `definition` and `text`. File paths MUST resolve to permitted inputs under {cite}`requirements.ci.input_containment`. Project-local paths SHOULD be recorded relative to the project for portability; absolute and parent-relative paths MAY be used when their resolved targets are permitted. `matches` MUST be an array of distinct full definition names, `hash` MUST be a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, and `text` MUST be a nonempty array of strings. Evidence MUST NOT store source text for outline inputs.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
:::{req} evidence_coverage
For every `{test}` reference in a project source file, including one in a
requirement or example declaration, the evidence file for the referenced
requirement or example MUST contain an input whose resolved source ranges cover
the reference's file and line. An `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{fixme}` reference alone
MUST NOT require an input selecting its source. `{impl}` and `{cite}` sources
remain discoverable through {cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`;
`{fixme}` acknowledgments are supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` and tracked by
{cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`. Habeas MUST report every uncovered
reference requiring coverage with its role, full name, source file, and line
number.
